title: API Token Controls
scope: Admin controls, logging and revocation for API credentials on SaaS platforms. Sourced from vendor documentation; not an audit of any tenant.

providers.name: Snowflake
providers.scope_notes: Avoid treating default PAT safeguards as immutable. Verify client/driver and cloud support for federation.

controls.name: Network policies (account / user / security integration)
controls.what: Restrict inbound access by IP or private endpoint; integration-level policy overrides user and account policies.
controls.setting: CREATE NETWORK POLICY; ALTER ACCOUNT/USER/SECURITY INTEGRATION SET NETWORK_POLICY
controls.quote: the most specific network policy overrides more general network policies.

controls.name: Snowflake OAuth integration ENABLED
controls.setting: ALTER SECURITY INTEGRATION ... SET ENABLED = FALSE
controls.quote: Specifies whether to initiate operation of the integration or suspend it.

controls.name: OAUTH_ISSUE_REFRESH_TOKENS / OAUTH_REFRESH_TOKEN_VALIDITY
controls.what: Turns refresh tokens off or sets their validity (custom clients 1 to 90 days, default 90).

controls.name: OAUTH_SINGLE_USE_REFRESH_TOKENS_REQUIRED
controls.what: Requires refresh tokens to be single-use.
controls.quote: Specifies whether single-use refresh tokens should be used.

controls.name: OAUTH_ENFORCE_PKCE
controls.what: Requires PKCE for every authorization instead of only when the client sends it.
controls.quote: we highly recommend that your client require PKCE for all authorizations.

controls_unknown: Edition requirements for authentication policies are not stated on the reference pages.
Whether Snowflake OAuth (as opposed to External OAuth) can be disallowed via AUTHENTICATION_METHODS; the OAUTH value is documented as 'Allows External OAuth'.
No account-wide policy found to force named key pairs or cap key-pair lifetime; legacy RSA_PUBLIC_KEY keys never expire.
Docs differ on how to unblock privileged roles for custom OAuth clients (account parameter vs Snowflake Support).
Whether the WIF quote 'disable it' covers the DEFAULT identity (docs say DEFAULT must use SET/UNSET WORKLOAD_IDENTITY).

authentication.summary: OAuth 2.0 with Snowflake as the authorization server. A partner or custom client sends the user through Snowflake sign-in and consent, then presents the short-lived Snowflake access token; refresh tokens are optional.

federation.details: Snowflake issues the tokens itself; no external token is exchanged. Tokens from an external authorization server use External OAuth (snowflake-5), and cloud workload identities use workload identity federation (snowflake-4).

ip_restriction.boundary: A network policy on the Snowflake OAuth integration covers code exchange, refresh token use and access token use, and overrides user and account policies. User-level policies are not checked on token requests (except the built-in local-application integration).

lifetime.summary: Default 10 min; configurable 1 min–1 h per integration

renewal.summary: Refresh tokens (on by default) default to 90 days (7776000 s); custom clients allow 1–90 days and partner apps 1 h–90 days, then the user must re-authorize. Single-use refresh tokens are optional.

administration.summary: Roles with CREATE INTEGRATION (ACCOUNTADMIN by default) create the integration. ACCOUNTADMIN, ORGADMIN, GLOBALORGADMIN and SECURITYADMIN are blocked by default; BLOCKED_ROLES_LIST, refresh-token settings and an integration network policy are set per integration.
administration.conditions: Avoid treating default PAT safeguards as immutable. Verify client/driver and cloud support for federation.

offboard.details: OAuth sessions run as a Snowflake user. Disabling that user, which SCIM deactivation does, aborts the user's queries and blocks new logins.

disable.cli: SQL: ALTER SECURITY INTEGRATION <name> SET ENABLED = FALSE

network.cli: SQL: ALTER SECURITY INTEGRATION <name> SET NETWORK_POLICY = '<np>'

expiry.cli: SQL: ALTER SECURITY INTEGRATION <name> SET OAUTH_ACCESS_TOKEN_VALIDITY = <secs> OAUTH_REFRESH_TOKEN_VALIDITY = <secs>

reads.cli: SQL: SELECT ... FROM SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE.ACCESS_HISTORY ah JOIN QUERY_HISTORY qh USING (query_id) JOIN LOGIN_HISTORY lh ON qh.authn_event_id = lh.event_id WHERE lh.authorizing_integration_name = '<INTEGRATION>'

offboard.ui: Snowsight > Governance & security > Users & roles > (user) ... > Disable User

token_format.notes: Access token and refresh token formats are not published. Access tokens last typically 10 minutes; refresh token life set by OAUTH_REFRESH_TOKEN_VALIDITY.

log_sources.name: SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE.LOGIN_HISTORY
log_sources.notes: Successful and failed logins, 365 days, up to 2h latency. INFORMATION_SCHEMA LOGIN_HISTORY table functions cover 7 days. OAuth logins have FIRST_AUTHENTICATION_FACTOR = OAUTH_ACCESS_TOKEN and AUTHORIZING_INTEGRATION_NAME = the security integration.

log_sources.name: SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE.SESSIONS
log_sources.notes: One row per session, 1 year, up to 3h latency; links to login via LOGIN_EVENT_ID. Does not track SQL API transient sessions. CLOSED_REASON includes OAUTH_CONSENT_REVOKED and OAUTH_CRITICAL_CHANGE_INTEGRATION.

log_sources.name: SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE.QUERY_HISTORY
log_sources.notes: Queries per SESSION_ID with AUTHN_EVENT_ID, 365 days, up to 45 min latency.

credential_id_fields.notes: Security integration (OAuth client) that granted access.
Links an OAuth session to its login event.

lifecycle_events.notes: FIRST_AUTHENTICATION_FACTOR value for OAuth logins, successful or failed.
Expired or invalid access token at session creation.
Refresh token invalid, expired, revoked, or issued to another client.

lifecycle_events.event: ALTER USER … REMOVE DELEGATED AUTHORIZATIONS FROM SECURITY INTEGRATION
lifecycle_events.notes: Revokes consent and associated OAuth access tokens.

anomaly_cues: OAuth login via an integration (AUTHORIZING_INTEGRATION_NAME) not normally used by that user
Same user's OAuth logins from two distant CLIENT_IPs within the token lifetime
OAuth sessions using a privileged ROLE_NAME after OAUTH_ADD_PRIVILEGED_ROLES_TO_BLOCKED_LIST was set to FALSE
New or altered OAuth security integration followed by logins from new IPs
Repeated invalid_grant / OAUTH_ACCESS_TOKEN_INVALID failures for one client

containment.steps: ALTER USER <u> REMOVE DELEGATED AUTHORIZATIONS FROM SECURITY INTEGRATION <int> (per user), or REMOVE DELEGATED AUTHORIZATIONS OF ANY ROLE FROM SECURITY INTEGRATION <int>; disable the integration (ENABLED = FALSE) for client-wide compromise; ALTER USER SET DISABLED = TRUE for user compromise.
containment.notes: ALTER USER docs say removal revokes OAuth access tokens for the integration, and SESSIONS has CLOSED_REASON OAUTH_CONSENT_REVOKED; whether all open sessions close is not stated.

sample_query.query: SELECT user_name, authorizing_integration_name, client_ip, COUNT(*) AS logins, MIN(event_timestamp) AS first_seen FROM SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE.LOGIN_HISTORY WHERE first_authentication_factor = 'OAUTH_ACCESS_TOKEN' AND is_success = 'YES' AND event_timestamp > DATEADD(day,-30,CURRENT_TIMESTAMP()) GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY first_seen DESC;
sample_query.purpose: Find new user/integration/IP combinations for Snowflake OAuth logins.

unknown: Audit record for refresh token issuance
